current.text: He joined Philadelphia after leaving the Lakers in free agency.
He is a projected starter next to Maxey, Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and Embiid.
Nick Nurse calls him an offense creator. Reports say he will play point guard and his job is to set up everyone else.
Philadelphia has very few backup bigs. Hukporti is out for the season, and Adem Bona and Tacko Fall are injured. It is an open question whether LeBron plays small-ball center.
He shares the ball with Maxey, Embiid and Jaylen Brown, so the team's stars will cut into each other's usage.
Experts project lower usage and under 20 points, but more assists. Josh expects a small rise in his on-ball role, with maybe 8 assists a game. One expert is a little worried about his efficiency.
Experts expect about 65 games, with planned games off. Mark expects load management for Philadelphia's stars.
He has always wanted to play big minutes, and Nurse may let him.
Expected to be a top 30 player per game.
Draft range: one expert says he is fine at pick 50 in category leagues and would go in the 40s in points leagues. Another says the 60s are fine, and the 50s too if you are not focused on turnovers.
His ESPN rank of 73 is called foolish, and going at 78 is far too low.
In auctions, Josh would not pay more than 25 USD. He went for 22 USD in an expert mock auction.
Philadelphia has only 13 back-to-backs, but three of them fall in the fantasy playoffs. The playoff schedule is 3-4-4 games with the March 28 end.
The low back-to-back total helps a little with his rest risk.
Mark projects Philadelphia for about 51 to 52 wins.

durable.text: He has sciatica and arthritis in his foot (arthritic toes). Sciatica bothered him last season.
These back and foot issues will cost him games off.
He is 41 and turns 42 this season.
Josh says his numbers stay about the same every season. His scoring drops, but he keeps the ball in his hands at a similar rate.
His assists are far above other forwards. His turnovers are a league outlier on the weak side.
He is worth more in points leagues than in 9-cat category leagues.

note: The sites disagree on his price. Yahoo values him at 24 USD (average cost 20.6 USD), ESPN at only 5 USD (average cost 16.6 USD), and he cost 22 USD in our league last season. Experts put the ceiling near 25 USD, so a price around 20 to 25 USD is fair, and he fits punt TO builds best because his turnovers (2.9 per game) are his one weak category and his forward-slot assists (6.8) are rare. Early on, check whether he really plays point guard and gets close to 8 assists, how many minutes Nurse gives him, and how often he sits for rest. Philadelphia has three back-to-backs in our playoff weeks.
